policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: The readings differ only in whether κατὰ σάρκα stands before or after κυρίοις; ASV recasts the phrase as a relative clause, 'them that according to the flesh are your masters', which renders either order.
The readings differ only in the article τοῦ before Χριστοῦ; English takes 'servants of Christ' with a bare proper name either way.

The candidates differ in punctuation, in the indefinite τι, and in where ἕκαστος stands; English must front the relative, and ASV 'whatsoever good thing each one doeth' gives τι no separate word, so it renders all four.
κομίσεται and κομιεῖται are the same future middle of κομίζω in its sigmatic and Attic forms; ASV 'shall he receive again' renders either.
The readings differ only in the article τοῦ before κυρίου; English requires 'the Lord' either way.
ASV 'he who is both their Master and yours' renders two coordinated genitives, αὐτῶν καὶ ὑμῶν; RP's ὑμῶν αὐτῶν is a single 'your own Master'.
ASV 'Finally, be strong in the Lord' has no vocative; RP's ἀδελφοί μου would give 'my brethren', and the note 'Or, Henceforth' fits the genitive of time τοῦ λοιποῦ.
ASV 'the world-rulers of this darkness' has one genitive; RP's added τοῦ αἰῶνος would give 'of the darkness of this world'.
ἐν and ἐπὶ with the dative πᾶσιν are both the adverbial 'in addition to all'; ASV renders it with the single word 'withal' either way.
The readings differ only in the article τὰ before πεπυρωμένα; ASV 'all the fiery darts of the evil one' makes the participle attributive with one article either way.
ASV 'And take the helmet of salvation' is imperative, rendering δέξασθε; RP's infinitive δέξασθαι would give 'to take'.
ASV 'and watching thereunto' renders εἰς αὐτό alone; RP's added τοῦτο is emphatic, and ASV writes it out where εἰς αὐτὸ τοῦτο stands at 6:22, 'for this very purpose'.
The readings differ only in whether εἰδῆτε precedes or follows καὶ ὑμεῖς; English fixes subject before verb, so ASV 'that ye also may know' renders either.
The readings differ only in the order of γνωρίσει and ὑμῖν; English fixes the verb before its indirect object, so ASV 'shall make known to you' renders either.
ASV ends the epistle at 'with a love incorruptible'; RP's added Ἀμήν would give a closing 'Amen'.
